content:
Last month, OpenAI teased hardware products under the Codex brand. Today, the company officially released its collaboration with Work Louder: the Codex Micro keyboard, priced at US$230.

The product introduction is as follows:

The keyboard comes in two versions: a clicky version and a silent version.

The website states: "Every Agent key lights up with different RGB lighting effects based on Codex's real-time status, so you can see at a glance which Agent is thinking, running, waiting, or has completed its work before switching conversations."

The product page also lists three Codex-exclusive features:

  • Instant skill triggers: flick the joystick to launch frequently used Codex workflows, such as reviewing PRs, debugging, or refactoring code.
  • Keep core operations at your fingertips: command keys provide dedicated shortcuts for your most frequent operations, including accept, reject, conversation keys, new conversations, and more. Reduce switching and boost efficiency.
  • Speak and it's done: turn the dial to instantly adjust reasoning intensity. Keep it fast for simple tasks, and crank it up when deeper thinking is needed.

You can order it here starting today. There's also a promo video:

That's about it. For OpenAI and the hardware space, this month has been quite eventful.
